prayerExcerpt.en-US: God never fails those who trust in Him; He guides them through darkness and through trials secretly and surely to their end, and in the evening time there is light.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Deus nunca falha àqueles que n'Ele confiam; Ele os guia através das trevas e das provações, secreta e seguramente, ao seu fim, e na hora da tarde haverá luz.

meta.face: A man of great age, well past a hundred, with a soft, pale, parchment-fine complexion and a SMALL, ROUND, SHRUNKEN face in which the mouth has FALLEN IN, bringing a small, HOOKED nose and a small, forward-CURVING chin close together (a gentle 'nutcracker' profile) — a round, BALD crown with a few wisps of fine white hair at the sides, small, soft, watery-blue eyes deep in folds of skin, puffed, softly drooping lids, sparse, long white brows, rounded, sunken cheeks; a SHORT, SPARSE, soft white beard that shows the chin's shape beneath; the gaze mild and trusting, the lips in a faint smile. Not the long, hatchet-faced simeon_jerusalem, the rosy, heart-shaped, full-haired polycarp, the long, tapering paul_hermit, the broad, flat-planed theodosius_cenobiarch or the round, flat-featured, long-bearded zephyrinus.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book and the Martyrology make him bishop in extreme old age (the Martyrology: 116 years at his death), so the card paints a very old man; the lamp is the book's Easter miracle of water turned to oil, told also by Eusebius (via Wikipedia).
